aggressive_definition: Incident advanced or lethal prostate cancer. The abstract separately analyzes postdiagnosis lethal/fatal outcomes and mortality among diagnosed patients, which are survival or progression outcomes rather than incidence.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: We used Cox proportional hazards models to examine traditional and alternative Med-Diet scores in relation to PCa incidence outcomes (advanced and lethal disease).
study_design: Prospective cohort analysis of incident advanced and lethal prostate cancer, plus a separate case-only postdiagnosis survival analysis.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We prospectively followed 47 867 men in the Health Professionals Follow-up Study followed from 1986 to 2010.
reason: The abstract explicitly analyzes incident advanced and lethal prostate cancer but does not analyze total prostate cancer incidence as an association endpoint. The 6,220 figure is the number of confirmed prostate cancer cases, while the supplied full-text evidence reports 1,032 advanced cases. The separate case-only analysis concerns postdiagnosis progression and mortality.
